purpose: Privacy-safe inventory of the attachment corpus referenced by the iCloud mail index. This records only aggregate metadata and recovery needs; it does not pretend metadata-only attachments were read.

filename_only_category_signals.note: These categories are non-exclusive keyword signals from filenames/extensions only. They identify future extraction targets and are not claims about document contents.

likely_value_of_future_extraction: Resume/CV versions could clarify education, skills, employment dates, and role descriptions with strong provenance.
Employment/HR documents could resolve job-history and onboarding details, but should be handled under a strict privacy boundary.
Housing/lease documents could resolve historical housing periods, but exact addresses and third-party data should remain local unless specifically needed.
Spreadsheets may contain structured personal planning data and could reveal reusable planning workflows.
Images/scans are the largest attachment class and may require OCR only after format-native extraction is unavailable.
E-books should be treated as reading/library artifacts rather than profile facts unless usage context makes them relevant.
extraction_policy: Recover attachment binaries from the original archive/provider or export pipeline.
Use format-native parsers for PDF/DOCX/XLSX/EPUB before OCR.
Use OCR only where necessary for image/scanned documents.
Keep raw binaries, extracted text, and sensitive source details local/private.
Link every extraction to message_id and attachment_id for provenance.
Run sensitivity detection before any model or Git promotion.
Promote only sanitized durable conclusions, never raw private documents.
current_boundary: Indexed message text is exhausted. Attachment recovery/analysis is implemented but the 231 metadata-only attachment bodies remain pending until the local machine re-fetches them from the configured iCloud account.

behavior: Re-fetches attachment-bearing indexed iCloud messages over read-only IMAP.
Extracts text from text/PDF/DOCX/XLSX/EPUB with format-native parsers.
Uses OCR only when explicitly requested and locally available.
Links each local result through source_id, message_id, and attachment_id.
Updates only the local mail index; no attachment body is automatically promoted to Git-backed profile state.
